## 9503c758d30f

**Semantic shortcut plus validator gap.** A rival can mark the four outer bounding-box corners of **every** color-6 component, without checking whether the component is a solid rectangle. It fits all **4/4 canonical pairs**, and ordinary generation only creates solid rectangles, so ordinary lessons never refute it.

I constructed an 8×8 input with one hollow 3×3 color-6 ring. The target `self_check` returns no findings even though the input violates the declared solid-rectangle invariant. The Racket authority leaves it unchanged; the rival paints four red corners. Across 120 ordinary draws (seeds 0–39, sample index `seed % 7`, 40 each in easy/medium/hard), zero contained a non-solid color-6 component.

The exact counterexample, 120-draw probe, hashes, outputs, and command are in `checks/audit-9503c758d30f-counterexample.json`. This input is outside the declared ordinary domain but inside the validator-accepted domain; the finding is therefore both a missing negative curriculum case and a weak-validator issue. No source was changed for this audit target.
